dd wishing you grace and peace paul made several missionary journeys to modern day greece and turkey (asia minor) establishing new christian communities. although he had to l eave the places after a relatively short time he never forgot the people and was constantly keeping up with their progress through the use of letters which we have today. he could admonish them if he heard the churches were deviating from what he taught or were getting caught up in petty politics (or worse). most of the time it was to encourage them. he complimented them on how they were progressing and he praised them in their hard work. encouragement is so important in lives. we all know what we should be doing but it is easier when people give us uplifting words. st teresa of kolkata said: “kind words can be short and easy to speak, but their echoes are truly endless. ” it can be easy to find fault in others and sometimes correction is necessary. but it is far more important to uplift people with words of encouragement! however, what adds to our pain isn't just our present situation also the burdens of the past. for some, it may be the behaviours and mistakes of last month, last week, or even further back.
for others, it may be a struggle with illness, which , even if successful, is quickly followed by another health scare or threat.
with a painful past and a dark present, it's understandable to feel little hope for the future.
this, however, is w here we get it wrong.
this sunday, jesus' parable makes it clear that our past and present needn't have the final say over our future.
those with a reputable history were denied the of sitting at the wedding banquet, whereas those with a colourful or chequered past found themselves in the wedding hall.
so, despite the difficulties of the present and our sometimes fraug ht lives, we should also be prepared for pleasant surprises in the future.
